body: I bought printer cartridges from an outside supplier for twenty four pounds because the office ran out before the delivery from our usual stockist arrived this week.
I drove to the regional office and back for the planning meeting, claiming mileage at the standard rate for forty two miles round trip.
The team ordered new headsets for the call centre and the total came to thirty eight pounds, which was paid up front on my card.
I was away overnight for the training course and I am claiming the standard daily subsistence allowance to cover meals during my stay.
I drove to the client site and back, claiming mileage at the usual rate, and I also paid thirty pounds to park near the venue for the day.
A few of us chipped in for cakes from the staff canteen to celebrate a colleague's birthday, and my share came to twelve pounds.
We used an external catering company for the client lunch meeting and the bill was eighteen pounds, which I paid myself and will claim back.
I am submitting the fixed daily allowance for my two days at the conference, and my actual spending on meals came to over thirty pounds each day.
The department needed a new subscription for the scheduling tool and it cost forty five pounds for the year, billed straight to my card.
I travelled to the two supplier visits in one day and I am claiming mileage at the company rate for the sixty miles I covered.
I ordered folders and labels from an outside stationery shop because the internal supply cupboard was empty, and the order came to nineteen pounds.
I picked up a book of stamps from reception for sending out a few letters and the cost was four pounds from petty cash.
The courier firm charged thirty two pounds to send the signed contracts overnight to the other office, and I paid this on my personal card.
I stayed over for the two day workshop and am claiming the standard subsistence allowance rather than itemising what I actually spent on food.
We had some name badges printed by an outside print shop for the open day and the order came to fifteen pounds including delivery.
Travelling out to the two branch offices this week, I am claiming mileage at the usual rate for the whole round trip.
I registered for the industry conference and the ticket price was fifty five pounds, which I paid myself ahead of the event.
I grabbed a coffee and a pastry from the staff kitchen before an early meeting and the total came to three pounds fifty.
I took a taxi from an outside firm to get to the airport for the early flight and the fare was twenty two pounds.
I am claiming the fixed overnight allowance for my stay near the client site rather than listing each individual meal I paid for.
The office needed a replacement kettle after the old one broke and I picked one up for twenty nine pounds from the shop.
Getting to the training venue and back in one day, I claimed mileage at the company rate for the eighty mile round trip.
An outside repair firm fixed the jammed shredder in the print room and charged twenty pounds for the call out and parts.
I borrowed a marker pen and a few sticky notes from the stationery cupboard and paid nine pounds towards a shared team order internally.
